focusQuestion: The 2026-08-14 baseline said the rotation was being vindicated, and told us to tighten the evidence-quality filter and treat “beat-and-raise, target held or cut” as the default expectation everywhere in the AI stack. Did that regime escalate, did the power/interconnect/packaging rotation destination hold — and, the question the baseline did not think to ask, has the binding constraint moved again?
authoringNote: Hand-authored from the source document, which is prose. Every number below traces to a line in Fab5_Cross_Source_Synthesis_20260905.md or its 6 September addendum. Nothing here is computed from price data and nothing is inferred beyond what the document states — the live technical strip on each ticker is the only measured content on this page, and it is joined in at build time from the same pipeline the other four tabs use. Where the source grades its own material that grade is carried; grade (a) is added here for company-reported prints and transacted prices, which the document treats as its strongest evidence but does not letter. The signal-board status buckets (confirmed / in motion / moved against / new) are this page's own grouping of the source's verbatim status labels, which are carried beside them.

evidenceHierarchy.title: Credit before equities — Run 6's monitoring order
evidenceHierarchy.note: The run's central methodological move is that the observable precursor is not a bankruptcy but spread widening in IG Tech while equities are still making highs. That specific divergence is what the current price structure would produce first, which is why credit is monitored ahead of equities. The sequencing is itself evidence: Red-Ring priced the signal on 24 August, ISI framed it four days later. Price preceded framework by four days, and that is worth watching for again.
rungs: Tenant-differentiated credit spreads — one physical asset, priced by who signs the lease
Single-name CDS at vendors guaranteeing their own customers' debt
IG Tech OAS against March's peak — ISI's formal fourth bear trigger
Equity multiples, which move last and are the easiest to argue away in real time

call.headline: Own the AI that funds itself; underweight the AI that has to borrow — and express the view through volatility, not direction.
call.body: Five houses converged on credit as the binding variable in ten days without citing each other. Red-Ring priced it first on 24 August — AVGO and NVDA CDS at all-time wides of 126.2bp and 86.7bp, and the tenant-yield split. ISI framed it four days later, swapping its fourth bear trigger from equities to IG Tech spreads, “the second most important chart there is.” TMTB structured it: Broadcom guaranteeing part of the senior tranche of the ~$100bn raise that funds its own largest customer. JPM turned it into a valuation instruction and Morgan Stanley supplied the counterparty arithmetic. When five houses converge on a variable in ten days without cross-citation, that variable is the one to trade. The expression is volatility because one Waller speech produced four readings across three houses spanning both directions, which is not resolvable by analysis before the event — layered on a dated correction window, a CTA book with 4.5x downside skew, and VIX at the fifth percentile.
call.notRecommended: This is not a reduction of AI exposure. Backlog cover is ~4x with sales revisions exceeding capex revisions; mega-cap tech is under-owned by 129bps and widening; SOX trades at 19.3x NTM, below the S&P's 19.5x; and the S&P ex-AI is up nearly 8% since late June — the AI complex has been a net drag, not an overheating source. Cutting gross exposure here would be trading the narrative rather than the evidence.

instructions.title: Long the self-funders against the balance-sheet-dependent tail
instructions.body: Emanuel's Low Leverage Leaders basket is already the right shape — NVDA, MU, AMD, PLTR, LRCX, ANET, MRVL, ALAB — ex-SpaceX, given that all three of its large AI compute contracts are cancelable on 90 days' notice. Per the 6 September addendum, “funds itself” must now be tested against hardware and capex exposure too, not only balance-sheet leverage.

instructions.title: Buy the September–January optionality rather than a direction
instructions.body: XLK one-month implied 23.6% against 27.7% realized, with VIX at 14.43. Long duration is the corroborating hedge, not a separate view — bond CTAs sit at −1.00 with +$223bn of DV01-equivalent buying on a −52bp rally, so risk-off gets double amplification.

instructions.title: Hold the memory trim at the un-contracted tier only, and size it small
instructions.body: Three houses are against it and one balanced source is half for it. The split is contracted versus un-contracted, not bull versus bear: UBS dates the DRAM top to 2Q28 and NAND to 4Q27, MS shows deficits of −4% to −17% through the horizon, NSR shows margins locked at floors — against Red-Ring's channel inventory moving ~1.5 → ~4 months.

whatChanged.headline: The binding constraint moved again — and every house moved with it independently.
whatChanged.body: Chip supply bound 2023–24. Power and cooling bound 2025 to mid-2026. From the second half of 2026 the binding constraint is credit. Fundamentals did not weaken — they strengthened almost everywhere this run looked. What changed is that the marginal dollar funding the buildout is now borrowed, increasingly by counterparties who are not hyperscalers, and the market has begun to price the difference.
whatChanged.stanceRefinement: One refinement from the 6 September addendum: “funds itself” must now be tested against hardware and capex exposure, not only balance-sheet leverage. Samsara is the instructive case — strong unit economics, accelerating ARR, and cash flow still took a 200bp hit because it buys physical devices.

bullets.title: The discount-rate shock
bullets.body: Ten- and thirty-year yields approached their 2007 highs on 18 August; semis fell 3.5% and the Nasdaq 1.2% on a day of universally good fundamental news. A simultaneous contraction in valuation and narrative, not in earnings — semis fell harder than software because semis are the concentrated carrier of AI crowding. Money exits the heaviest position, not the most expensive valuation. US public debt crossed $40.047trn.

bullets.title: The capex ladder goes up again, on all rungs
bullets.body: UBS raised top-12 hyperscaler capex 9%/27% to $998bn/$1,447bn/$1,612bn (2026/27/28E) and lifted WFE a third consecutive time to $158/$226/$274.5bn. ISI raised its 2027 WFE base case to $215bn from $180bn. NSR published the highest number anywhere — $450bn of 2026 AI-infrastructure capex and $3tn by 2030. TSMC's 2026 revenue guide moved from “above 30%” to “slightly above 40%”. Inside the same week, ISI's Lipacis reported DRAM brokers discounting into franchise distributors, contradicting his own colleague's memory-inflation preview. Neither analyst referenced the other.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole — Warsh more hawkish than the pre-read
bullets.body: 2% PCE a “firm, fixed target”; 54% of PCE items above 3%, which UBS independently replicated at 53%; an explicit refusal to credit long yields as restraint; closing on “committed to a discipline, not to a decision.” He named AI as a possible new factor of production and cited the two leading labs' combined annualised token sales above $100bn, up more than 500% y/y — without using productivity to justify easing.

bullets.title: NVIDIA deletes the demand debate
bullets.body: FY28 guided roughly +70% (~$680–700bn), about ten points above even the most optimistic buy-side bogey of 60%. Data centre reached 93% of revenue, with ACIE (+138% y/y) growing faster than Hyperscale (+102%) — the buyer base is broadening. Two disclosures matter more than the guide: gross margin guided to a 71–72% trough in FQ4:27 on memory inflation the company cannot fully offset, and supply commitments jumping $119bn → $279bn (+114% q/q), “a large portion” of it memory.

bullets.title: Earnings adjudicate on quality, not on beats
bullets.body: DELL's traditional server and networking revenue rose 122% y/y against +96% expected, FY27 guidance raised from “slightly above 60%” to “over 100%”. Apple's clean gross margin fell ~48.1% → ~46.5% despite a $150–250 ASP increase. On the same 3 September tape, Broadcom fell 4%, NetApp 9% and HPE 5% on numbers that were beautiful but whose quality was in doubt. Credo's target was cut 10.2% in the same week it raised its own growth guide.

bullets.title: The software blowout
bullets.body: Software outperformed semis by ~5pts on NVIDIA's +9% print day. OKTA +29%, CRM +22%, CRWD +20% on net-new-ARR and cRPO beats that broke a defensively positioned book. Dario Amodei appeared on the Salesforce call alongside Benioff. Marvell fell 5% despite raising its FY27 guide to $12.0bn and FY28 to $18.0bn — the 3Q gross-margin guide of 58.0% against 58.5% expected dominated.

bullets.title: The macro gate opens, then half-closes
bullets.body: ISI reversed its own call on 28 August — September FOMC live for a hike at ~50% — hardened it on 31 August, added oil as a second independent trigger on 1 September as WTI moved close to $90, then resolved dovishly on 3 September when Waller proposed a materially looser three-month-annualised test. August payrolls printed +162,000 against ISI's own +70k preview: stronger but not hotter. Two supertankers were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on 1 September.

bullets.title: The credit tape starts pricing tenant quality
bullets.body: Broadcom is raising more than $60bn senior plus roughly $30bn subordinated through an Apollo/Blackstone SPV, with Broadcom itself guaranteeing part of the senior tranche. Nebius's $4.5bn convertible dragged CoreWeave down 4% and Oracle 3% — the first time AI financing dilution priced as a sector factor. Alphabet paid its highest-ever coupon (6.98%) despite A$18bn of demand. And NVIDIA quietly cut its OpenAI Ohio backstop 52%, from ~$250bn to under $120bn — and the market did not reprice it.

bullets.title: Memory inflation surfaces downstream
bullets.body: Zscaler and Samsara both cut cash-flow guidance and named the same cause. ZS takes FY27 capex/revenue from 8% to low-double-digits on memory, storage and processor prices with supply tightening; IOT cuts FY27 FCF margin ~200bp to ~12% on component and freight inflation, persisting into 2027. Bernstein's 3Q26 prints (~+19% DRAM, ~+20% NAND) sit inside the band already carried. Microsoft moved to challenge Virginia's transmission pre-payment rule — the first hyperscaler to fight a state cost order.

layers.title: Operational fundamentals
layers.summary: Stronger than Run 5, with the constraint moved downstream of the fab. Cloud backlog approaching $1.7trn on ISI's count against forward cloud capex just over $620bn — roughly 4x cover, with sales revisions exceeding capex revisions. AWS +37% at a record 39.4% operating margin; Google Cloud +82% with margin 20.7% → 35.6%. What binds is conversion, not demand: Amazon's raise from $200bn to $220bn was entirely memory inflation with zero incremental capacity, and DELL says upside is limited by memory/SSD supply and site readiness, not demand. The 2027 question has been rewritten from “can you get the order” to “can you light the equipment up.”

layers.title: Market structure
layers.summary: Genuinely contradictory, and both halves are real. Bullish: mega-cap tech under-owned by 129bps versus the S&P and widening; ETF shorts covering a sixth straight week; the S&P ex-AI up nearly 8% since late June while the index ranged — the AI complex has been a net drag. SOX at 19.3x NTM, below the S&P's 19.5x. Bearish: CFTC non-dealer Nasdaq positioning turned negative for the first time since May 2025 on a record −$21bn week, during a +7% rally. Ten stocks are 38% of the S&P against a 27% dot-com peak, with three-month implied correlation at generational lows. Extreme concentration plus low correlation is mathematically fragile, and the rotation Run 5 called for has been happening inside the complex rather than out of it.

layers.title: Financing and credit
layers.summary: This is where the run's information is, and five houses reached it independently in ten days without cross-citation. Red-Ring priced it first on 24 August — AVGO and NVDA CDS at all-time wides of 126.2bp and 86.7bp — and ISI framed it four days later, swapping its fourth bear trigger from equities to IG Tech credit spreads. The cleanest signal is the tenant split: AMZN-tenant data-centre bonds at 5.9–6.5% YTW against CoreWeave/NVDA-tenant paper at 8–9%. Price signal preceded framework by four days, which is worth watching for again.

layers.title: Macro and policy
layers.summary: An unresolvable September and a 2027 collision. On 3 September, reading the same Waller speech: GS put hike odds at ~60%, ISI at “under 50 per cent”, and TMTB read it as a priced cut with ~60% odds of action within weeks — the same number, opposite directions. ISI's three-wave inflation model now names AI capex at ~2pp of the ~53% July diffusion index, with the channel identified explicitly as memory-chip costs. That is the first time in this project's history that the AI capex cycle appears as a quantified input to the Fed's reaction function rather than as a sector story.

insights.headline: The third migration — the binding constraint is now credit
insights.claim: Chip supply bound 2023–24, power and cooling bound 2025 to mid-2026, and from the second half of 2026 the binding constraint is credit. TMTB states it explicitly; four other houses arrive at it by their own routes.
insights.evidence: Five houses reached credit independently in ten days without cross-citation. Red-Ring priced CDS at all-time wides on 24 August — AVGO 126.2bp, NVDA 86.7bp. ISI made IG Tech OAS its formal fourth bear trigger four days later, calling it “the second most important chart there is.” JPM turned it into a valuation instruction and MS supplied the counterparty arithmetic.

priorRun.predicted: “AI financing circularity is now a standing risk, not an isolated one — the third instance should be treated as confirmation of a pattern, not a new surprise.”
priorRun.outcome: Five houses reached credit independently in ten days without cross-citation; Red-Ring priced it and ISI formalised it as a bear trigger four days later.

insights.headline: Capex has stopped being a proxy for demand
insights.claim: A rising share of incremental capex is swallowed by memory inflation rather than converted into capacity. Track GW, not dollars.
insights.evidence: Amazon's 31 July raise from $200bn to $220bn bought zero incremental GW. NVIDIA's own margin guide names memory inflation it cannot fully offset. DELL names memory/SSD supply and site readiness rather than demand as the limit on upside.

priorRun.predicted: Nothing on this. Run 5 asked whether spend could be powered, financed and margin-translated — it did not anticipate that capex would stop measuring demand at all.
priorRun.outcome: Established this run by three independent routes: Amazon's raise with zero incremental capacity, NVIDIA's margin guide, and DELL naming supply rather than demand as the constraint.

insights.headline: Targets are now cut on beats, not merely held
insights.claim: The beat-and-raise, hold-the-target regime escalated past holding. The escape valve is an accelerating growth rate or a new quantified AI disclosure.
insights.evidence: ADI $474 → $462 on a clean beat-and-raise; AVGO cut on a beat with CY27 EPS cut 7.5%; CIEN's target cut 31.8% while FY27 EPS was raised 24% above Street; and Credo cut 10.2% in the same week it raised its own guide, P/E compressing 34x to 23x — the cleanest instance recorded anywhere in this project.

priorRun.predicted: Indicator #29's bearish trigger: “The pattern spreads further … or deepens (targets get cut, not just held, on beats).”
priorRun.outcome: The trigger fired, on four named instances inside three weeks.

insights.headline: GPUs outlive the depreciation schedule
insights.claim: The residual-value dispute resolves bullish — but the sample is non-hyperscaler clouds only, and rental prices depend on supply tightness, generational efficiency and power prices.
insights.evidence: A 2020-vintage A100 still rents at $1.65/hr on a ~$5,000 residual, against B200 at $5.61 on ~$70,000. CoreWeave has extended A100 contracts to 2029. Silicon Data's rental series held through the window.

priorRun.predicted: Carried as a bear trigger: “the power/site-scarcity reattribution is confirmed, undermining the chip residual-value framing entirely.”
priorRun.outcome: It resolved against the bear. Both mechanisms operate and the reattribution is not vindicated as an exclusive explanation, so #6 and #28 stay split rather than merged and the audit trail survives.

insights.headline: The market did not reprice the backstop cut
insights.claim: NVIDIA cut its OpenAI Ohio backstop 52%, from ~$250bn to under $120bn for the first ~5GW phase, and the market barely moved. The run's most important unpriced variable.
insights.evidence: Neoclouds moved +1.71% against +13.6% on the original announcement — an eight-fold amplitude contraction on a disclosure of the same structure.

priorRun.predicted: The metric, not the direction: “track NVDA's 10-Q disclosure of backstop and guarantee balances — the pace of that climb is the single best real-time gauge of how aggressively the structure is being used.”
priorRun.outcome: The balance moved the other way and the market did not react. Run 5 had the right instrument and the wrong sign.

insights.headline: “AI destroys seats” was falsified twice in one day
insights.claim: On 27 August, Salesforce reported Sales, Service and Slack seats all growing y/y and Okta said there is no evidence AI is reducing seats. Microsoft then chose a $99/month seat bundle to carry agent governance.
insights.evidence: Two independent falsifications on one day, plus — from the 6 September addendum — Okta accelerating 29% with no meaningful AI revenue at all, the cleanest control case available, and Zscaler disclosing non-seat pricing at ~30% of new-and-upsell ACV, the first hard quantification in this project.
sources: Barclays and BTIG via TMTB Addendum

priorRun.predicted: The opposite. Run 5 carried agents-reduce-seats as the working frame.
priorRun.outcome: Falsified twice on one day. This read is a falsification of the project's own prior, not a confirmation of it.

insights.headline: The bottleneck migrated past ABF
insights.claim: TSMC's own VP closed the CoWoS dispute toward tightness, but the live constraints are further upstream: InP substrate, cleanroom availability, advanced-node SoC allocation — and skilled electricians, which only Red-Ring names.
insights.evidence: TSMC's VP of Advanced Packaging named ABF substrate and memory shortages persisting “over the next couple of years.” The addendum extends it: Lumentum pulled NPO commercialisation forward a full year, from end-2028/early-2029 to end-2027/early-2028, and now expects NPO to be larger than CPO.

priorRun.predicted: Indicator #20's bullish trigger: “ABF substrate capacity data resolves the dispute toward continued tightness.”
priorRun.outcome: The trigger fired on TSMC's own VP, and the addendum extended it a year forward on the optical timetable.

insights.headline: Target prices are a corrupted signal
insights.claim: Read the EPS revision and the horizon, never the headline target. Two houses reached the corrupted-signal conclusion independently.
insights.evidence: Inside ISI, nine hours apart: numbers cut and target held for +58.7% upside, against numbers raised 24% and target cut a third for +5.9% — a 53-point spread in implied upside, same buildout, same firm, same day, neither note acknowledging the other. JPM independently warns five names changed target horizon at the same time as target price.

priorRun.predicted: That “beat-and-raise, hold-the-target” had formalised as the default expectation and was spreading into semicap for the first time.
priorRun.outcome: It escalated past holding to cutting, and then appeared inside a single house on a single day.

insights.headline: State restriction is bullish behind-the-meter
insights.claim: Moratoria raise on-site generation demand because the grid cannot carry the load. “Going fully BTM is the insulation trade.”
insights.evidence: 300+ state bills in six weeks and Texas suspending ~1,800 data centres, with the restriction impulse explicitly non-partisan. MS reframes community opposition as “a development constraint that needs to be underwritten like land, power or labor.” The addendum adds the first hyperscaler to contest a state cost order — Microsoft, in Virginia.

priorRun.predicted: The sign the other way. Indicator #27's bearish trigger was “permitting politics worsen.”
priorRun.outcome: Run 6 inverts it — worsening politics is bullish for behind-the-meter generation, on ISI's inverted read plus MS's underwriting frame.

agreement.claim: Memory pricing is at or near record, and near-term prints are still rising.
agreement.detail: DRAM gross margin 87% and NAND 80% — all-time highs; DRAM ASPs +5x and NAND +4x since 1Q25; 18 consecutive weeks of spot increases; export prices +135% y/y in 1H26.

agreement.claim: Power is the physical binding constraint and holds the margin pool.
agreement.detail: Two unrelated ISI desks reached this independently in the same week without citing each other. NSR: “grid capacity, not chip supply, is emerging as the scarcest resource.”

agreement.claim: The Marvell $120bn headline is a ceiling, not a base case.
agreement.detail: JPM, NSR and MS reached this independently: it is warrant-implied commercial stickiness, not RPO, and explicitly not a core TPU accelerator order. NSR's own 2028 estimate is ~$10bn. Only the market read it as displacement.

agreement.claim: Custom silicon versus GPU is not zero-sum.
agreement.detail: MS's CoWoS allocation build has NVIDIA at 780k wafers (2026e) → 1,222k (2027e), Broadcom 300k → 484k and AMD 60k → 530k — all three scaling simultaneously. The constraint is packaging capacity, not competitive share.

agreement.claim: Credit is the new binding constraint.
agreement.detail: Reached in sequence by Red-Ring (price), ISI (framework), TMTB (structure) and JPM (valuation instruction) — without cross-citation.

scenarios.name: Base case
scenarios.body: Fundamentals keep printing well, the tape keeps discriminating on quality rather than on beats, and the index goes nowhere in particular while dispersion stays violent. September's 17 investor days mean price action is driven by company-set multi-year targets rather than quarterly results — the same fact that made the last six weeks a target-cutting regime. Rotation continues inside the complex: quality balance sheets over levered growth, adopters over builders, upstream over integrators.
triggers: IG Tech OAS holding inside March's peak

scenarios.name: Bull case
scenarios.body: The 30-year breaks stably below 5% and, on BofA's explicit formulation, the persistent underperformance of AI capex spenders and builders versus adopters ends.
triggers: The 30-year through 5% on a sustained basis
Micron's print confirming the ~50% HBM price increase with pricing detail
Anthropic's S1 validating the value-chain economics
Broadcom's ~$100bn raise pricing tight and heavily subscribed

scenarios.name: Bear case
scenarios.body: Not the usual 10–15%, because ISI's window is dated: each of the past six cycles saw a mid-cycle correction within four months of industry y/y revenue peaking, and the second derivative peaks in the Sep-26 quarter — so the window is September 2026 to January 2027, uncontested by any other source.
triggers: IG Tech OAS widening beyond March's peak — ISI's formal fourth bear trigger
Channel inventory extending past four months

scenarios.name: Base case
scenarios.body: The buildout continues at a scale nobody in this project has yet had to mark down, and returns accrue where they have been accruing — to the power layer, to upstream enablers, to vendors who can self-finance, and to memory makers whose contracts are locked. Compute capacity roughly quadruples to ~120GW by 2028 on MS's numbers. The 2027 constraint is energisation, not orders, and the buyer base keeps broadening — which reduces dependence on a few hyperscalers while raising the dispersion of customer credit quality.

scenarios.name: Bull case
scenarios.body: The AI-disclosure multiple generalises. A quantified AI contribution earns roughly three-plus turns of EV/sales and near-zero without one — Snowflake 9.3x → 12.4x and held; Datadog 10.9x → 13.9x → 16.9x; MongoDB zero turns on a solid AI-silent quarter. If more of the complex can produce per-SKU quantified disclosure, the multiple compression of the last six weeks reverses with no change in fundamentals.

scenarios.name: Bear case
scenarios.body: ISI's ADI analog: once NTM EPS clears the prior cycle peak by a low-double-digit percentage, the multiple historically absorbs the beats — 38% and 60% compression after 15% and 11% overshoots. This cycle's overshoot is 30% with only 29% compression so far. If the analog holds, the correction is a multiple event with earnings still rising — the hardest kind to trade and the easiest to argue away in real time.

bearCase.headline: The thesis does not break on a demand miss. It breaks if financing reverses before fundamentals stall.
bearCase.body: Red-Ring identifies the mechanism: the platform migrates GPU residual value, utilisation, customer credit and re-lease risk into private credit, insurance money and project finance — creating the possibility that multiple financing vehicles mark down residual value and tighten leverage simultaneously, forcing project cancellations into an order book that is still nominally strong. Morgan Stanley identifies the counterparty: CoreWeave tenant debt to $116.2bn by 2028, with tenant-level leverage compounding faster than the assets are being de-risked. TMTB identifies the correlated structure: Broadcom guaranteeing part of the senior tranche of the debt that funds its own largest customer, so an Anthropic disappointment produces falling orders and guarantee payouts at once. The observable precursor is not a bankruptcy — it is spread widening in IG Tech while equities are still making highs.

variants.title: The slower break — cost-push ASP inflation
variants.body: Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell system prices are reportedly up ~15–17% attributed to DRAM cost, and NVIDIA's own gross margin troughs at 71–72% on memory it cannot fully offset. Broadcom's MW gross margin is modelled falling 77.3% → 67.4% by FY28e. If ASP inflation is cost-push rather than value-add, gross margin and customer ROI become the next constraint. Volume growth is no longer automatically converting into margin expansion anywhere in the hardware stack.

variants.title: The multiple version — Lipacis's ADI analog
variants.body: Once NTM EPS clears the prior cycle peak by a low-double-digit percentage, the multiple has historically done the work of absorbing the beats — 38% and 60% compression after 15% and 11% overshoots. This cycle's overshoot is 30% with only 29% compression to date. The framework implies AVGO at $283–$174 against Lipacis's own published bear case of $341, and the note does not acknowledge the conflict.

variants.title: And what would kill the recommendation
variants.body: IG Tech spreads tightening decisively through 100bp while the tenant-quality spread compresses. That would say the credit market has looked at the vendor-financing structures and decided they are additive capital rather than relocated leverage — NSR's case. If it happens, drop the short leg and stay long the complex outright.

calendar.body: September FOMC — into a market where one speech produced four readings across three houses, spanning both directions. The single largest source of near-term volatility, and the reason the recommendation is expressed through optionality.
17 investor days. Price action will be driven by company-set multi-year targets, not quarterly results — the same fact that made the last six weeks a target-cutting regime.
BEA revision — ISI expects it to lower reported core PCE by ~20bp. Note the sequencing: it lands after the FOMC, so the meeting is decided on the unrevised number.

Micron's next print — the decisive evidence on conflict ①. Specifically whether the ~50% HBM price increase appears with pricing detail in company commentary, rather than as NSR's back-solve from NVIDIA's margin give-back.
Meta's Hatch/PSI gate — the first verification of the agent-productivity thesis. Track task success rate, trust incidents, paid conversion and inference cost per task, not headline availability.
CME compute-futures launch — the second independent price signal on GPU rental economics, against Silicon Data's marks.
Marvell investor day — whether it confirms the >30% attach trajectory and stands behind the raised FY28 $18.0bn guide and 60% data-centre growth.
Texas governor's audit of ~300 data centres reports. The most specific date on the state-politics indicator, against a backdrop of ~1,800 suspended approvals.
Micron's CHIPS Act restrictions expire, enabling ~100% FCF return. This also partially reconciles the Micron buyback contradiction that has run unresolved across seven consecutive UBS batches.

Gemini 3.8 Flash introductory pricing is scheduled to double. ISI reads it correctly as an adoption subsidy — and it is the cleanest scheduled test of whether token deflation is structural or promotional.
Samsung board meeting — the next Korea capital-allocation catalyst, pushed out from this run.
ISI's mid-cycle correction window closes. Uncontested by any other source this run.
ERCOT “Batch Zero” — ~200GW under review, already slipping past this date.

The debt-limit collision — $39.9tn against a $41.1tn ceiling, roughly $1tn of headroom against ~$2tn of annual net borrowing. Sovereign supply, a debt-ceiling standoff and $1.3tn of hyperscaler capex financing on the same long-end bid. Also the first tradeable moment on the memory-hierarchy roadmap.

Anthropic's S1. The single highest-information event pending — the first hard check on the value-chain estimates (~20% of tokens, ~85% of revenue, >90% of gross profit), on the $11.5–11.6bn Q2 figure that is currently media-reported rather than audited, and on a company that is simultaneously Broadcom's largest FY27 customer.
Broadcom's ~$100bn raise prices. Watch the subscription and the spread on the AVGO-guaranteed senior tranche — the most direct read available on conflict ⑦.

The two disclosures that matter more than the guide both cut the other way: gross margin guided to a 71–72% trough in FQ4:27 on memory it cannot fully offset, and supply commitments $119bn → $279bn (+114% q/q). NVDA is now the credit anchor of the whole edifice, and it quietly cut the OpenAI Ohio backstop 52% without the market repricing it.

The single clearest expression of the run's thesis, on both legs. CDS at an all-time wide of 126.2bp; a ~$100bn raise through an Apollo/Blackstone SPV with AVGO itself guaranteeing part of the senior tranche of the debt that funds its own largest customer; ~15 of 20GW of the FY28 pipeline from Anthropic and OpenAI. The next print is the decisive evidence on the memory cycle-top conflict — specifically whether the ~50% HBM increase appears with pricing detail rather than as a back-solve.

The clearest evidence that custom silicon versus GPU is not zero-sum: MS's CoWoS allocation build has AMD going 60k wafers (2026e) → 530k (2027e) while NVIDIA and Broadcom also scale. Inference CPU:GPU shifting 1:4 → 1:1 is the second leg. In Emanuel's Low Leverage Leaders basket — the self-funder side of the recommendation.

Two quantities both read as “120” and are a factor of ten apart: the $120bn Google headline is warrant-implied commercial stickiness, a demand ceiling and not RPO, while the FY27 company revenue guide is $12.0bn (raised from $11.5bn) with FY28 raised to $18.0bn. The stock fell 5% on the raise anyway — the 3Q gross-margin guide of 58.0% against 58.5% expected dominated. The 6 October investor day is the checkpoint.

JPM's caution is the counterweight: “2x capacity by 2028” is an option, not a TAM forecast, and extrapolating it misreads supply willingness as confirmed demand. Cleanroom availability, not tools, is the binding constraint.

On the substance CIEN settles the shape of the optics risk — it refutes the demand bear case and confirms the pricing bear case by omission, so FY27–28 is a margin risk, not a volume risk.

The optical timetable moved forward a full year: NPO now expected to be larger than CPO, with commercialisation pulled from end-2028/early-2029 to end-2027/early-2028. Undershipping by more than 30% with all EML capacity under LTAs through CY2027. OCS is repricing from network component to compute-availability insurance, against $20–40m of compute-time value at risk per deployment.

Sold out through FY27 and doubling InP epi capacity by end-F1Q27 and again by end-2027 — but with FY26 operating cash flow of ~$80m against $1.10bn of capex. A self-funding test case in the addendum's sense: the unit economics are not the question, the cash conversion is. Corroborating LITE's NPO pull-forward is the bullish trigger on indicator #20.

Traditional server and networking revenue +122% y/y against +96% expected, FY27 guidance raised from “slightly above 60%” to “over 100%”, with management explicitly naming agentic workloads. Also the cleanest statement of the run's constraint: upside is limited by memory/SSD supply and site readiness, not demand.

Fell 5% on the 3 September tape on numbers that were beautiful but whose quality was in doubt — one of the three same-day instances (with AVGO −4% and NTAP −9%) that established earnings now adjudicate on quality rather than on beats.
Fell 9% on 3 September on a beat — the largest of the three same-day quality repricings, and the reason the run treats a beat as insufficient information about the next day's price.

The vehicle for the only new memory-valuation argument this run: BofA applies SanDisk's ~80% gross-margin structure to Micron, which moves memory's margin structure toward software and asks the market to abandon cyclical low multiples. It is a parallel argument to NSR's Price/COGS, not a corroboration of it.

Sits on both new indicators. On seats versus tokens it chose a $99/month seat bundle to carry agent governance, and the E7 bundle holding or converting to consumption is the bellwether. On state politics it became the first hyperscaler to contest a state cost order, challenging Virginia's transmission pre-payment rule. AI-infra steady-state ROIC modelled at ~21–27%.

Dragged down 3% by Nebius's $4.5bn convertible — the first time AI financing dilution priced as a sector factor rather than a single-name event. The open question on the other side is whether ORCL-style pre-contracting, with 98% of AI capacity already committed, caps upside rather than de-risking it.

Half of the 27 August falsification of “AI destroys seats”: Sales, Service and Slack seats all growing y/y, +22% on the print, with Dario Amodei appearing on the call alongside Benioff. A seat-count decline attributable to agents at CRM would be the bearish trigger on indicator #30.
+20% on net-new-ARR and cRPO beats that broke a defensively positioned book, in the 28 August software blowout that outperformed semis by ~5pts on NVIDIA's own +9% print day.

The name that carries both addendum findings at once. It gave memory cost inflation a documented downstream free-cash-flow channel — FY27 capex/revenue taken from 8% to low-double-digits explicitly on memory, storage and processor prices — and it disclosed non-seat pricing at ~30% of new-and-upsell ACV, the first hard quantification of the seats-versus-tokens mix in this project.

The instructive case behind the stance refinement: strong unit economics and accelerating ARR, and FY27 FCF margin still cut ~200bp to ~12% on component and freight inflation persisting into 2027 — because it buys physical devices. “Funds itself” has to be tested against hardware and capex exposure, not only leverage.

The symmetric case on the AI-disclosure multiple: 10.9x → 13.9x → 16.9x EV/sales as quantified AI disclosure accumulated, and −19% on disclosed concentration. Roughly three-plus turns for a quantified AI contribution, near-zero without one, with a real penalty attached.

Google Cloud +82% with operating margin 20.7% → 35.6% on the fundamental side, against the run's cleanest single credit datum on the other: Alphabet paid its highest-ever coupon at 6.98% despite A$18bn of demand. MS also flags its own unresolved GOOGL target — $415 on 12 July against $400 in the 17 August boilerplate, with no dedicated note in the window.

Both halves of the run in one name. AWS +37% at a record 39.4% operating margin — and the 31 July capex raise from $200bn to $220bn bought zero incremental GW, which is the evidence that capex has stopped being a proxy for demand. Amazon-tenant data-centre bonds at 5.9–6.5% YTW are the investment-grade side of the tenant split.

The ~$17bn youth-safety settlement, about 1% of revenue, removes one of two overhangs and is framed as a GOOGL-style clearing event, with META trading 25% below its own long-term multiple. Against it: ~$347bn of leases not yet commenced, and an ROI that has split into a proven ad cash cow and an unproven high-capital option. Hatch/PSI is the first verification gate.

The consumer end of memory de-spec, and the evidence that the “high end is immune” assumption is broken: clean gross margin fell ~48.1% → ~46.5% despite a $150–250 ASP increase, with the largest-ever Pro price hikes modelled specifically to offset memory. Smartphone units −14% y/y is the steepest ever recorded.
